newsitem.title: INDIA: Fiat expects nod soon on India car deal.
newsitem.headline: Fiat expects nod soon on India car deal.

text.p: Italy's Fiat Spa said on Thursday that it expects the Indian government to approve its proposal "very soon" to set up a joint car-making company with a local partner.
"I expect the approval to come very soon...any time now," Fiat's representative in India, Franco Pilastro, told Reuters in New Delhi.

Fiat has proposed setting up a joint venture with the Vinod Doshi family, which controls India's Premier Automobiles Ltd, to manufacture Fiat's Palio model in India. Premier already makes Fiat's Uno model in India under licence.
Pilastro said Fiat would start investing in India as soon as the Foreign Investment Promotion Board approved the proposal.
"Fiat is interested in investing in the range of $1.2 billion dollars in various projects in India," he said, saying the investments would come over the next five years.
Pilastro said the car project would constitute a major share of the proposed investment but the company had plans to invest in other projects too.
"There are many projects that Fiat wants to invest in but Fiat Auto's proposal to manufacture cars is the biggest one with an initial investment of nearly $300 million," he said.
Fiat would have a 74 percent stake in the proposed joint venture, while the Doshi family would hold the remaining equity.

The two firms plan to build a new plant near the western city of Pune with a capacity to manufacture 100,000 Palio cars a year. The proposed joint venture hopes to begin production at the new plant in mid-1999.
Indian analysts project the domestic car market in the second most populous nation to grow to around one million units in 2000/2001 (April-March) from 345,355 in 1995/96.
Pilastro said Fiat unit New Holland was planning to invest some $50 million to build tractors in India.
Fiat also has a tie-up with Ashok Leyland through its company Iveco to make trucks in India.
Last month auto component maker Magnetti Marelli, part of the Fiat group, announced a joint venture with PAL for development, manufacture and sale of auto components.

India's auto sector has already attracted majors like U.S.-based Ford Motor Co and General Motors Corp, France's Peugeot and South Korea's Daewoo after opening its market under an economic reform programme launched in 1991.
The companies are competing with Maruti Udyog Ltd, a joint venture between Japan's Suzuki Motor Co and the Indian government, which has a 70 percent share of the Indian car market.
